What kind of containers? virtual containers that host things similar to VMs? Or things like shipping containers?

Virtual containers. I don't know much of anything about the other containers except they are boxes (spheres, cubes, rectangles...) made of various materials.

Containers are similar to virtual machines. Except they do not require their own operating systems to run. They use the host operating system as their OS mostly, by using them in a read only format. Many will copy system system libraries that they need write access to into the container as part of it's package. Containers provide a lightweight way to run an application, as they do not include an entire operating system in the package. Usually only specific application code, system libraries, and dependencies will be part of the container itself. Executing this code on the host OS kernel. By not using a full OS for each application like a virtual machine does, they save memory on the host system by not running many copies of the same OS.

Docker and RedHat Openshift, are examples of container services that manage container deployment. Kubernetes is an example of a service that is designed to manage container orchestration.

Docker has specific things like swarm mode that allows for managing a group of containers as a single unit.

A quick delineation of whether to use a virtual machine or a container is do you want a system that hosts one specific application or function, or do you require one capable of hosting multiple functions.

This is obviously only a quick overview, and for more in depth reading I would suggest you look into the links below. https://docs.docker.com/

https://docs.openshift.com/index.html

https://kubernetes.io/docs/home/

Download and install a container service and then you create them yourself. You do not need others to do any of this for you. The container services are already out there. Whether you run Linux (suggested) or Windows, you can install Docker and then start building them yourself.

Figure out what you want to run and then build a container that does that specific thing.
That is the goal of a container. Making it small.
